{{Short description|Codebreaker at Bletchley Park (1923–2020)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}{{Use British English|date=April 2025}}

'''Joan Winifred Joslin''' ({{née}} '''Glover''', 11 March 1923 – 8 February 2020) was an English [[Cryptanalysis|codebreaker]] at [[Bletchley Park]] during [[World War II]].

== Early life ==
Joslin was born as Joan Glover on 11 March 1923 in [[Staffordshire]], England.<ref name=":0">{{cite web |last=Bearne |first=Suzanne |date=24 July 2018 |title=Meet the female codebreakers of Bletchley Park |url=https://www.theguardian.com/careers/2018/jul/24/meet-the-female-codebreakers-of-bletchley-park |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230705040952/https://www.theguardian.com/careers/2018/jul/24/meet-the-female-codebreakers-of-bletchley-park |archive-date=5 July 2023 |website=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref>

== Career ==
Joslin was ordered to Bletchley Park on 24 December 1941.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> During her initial interview, she took tests and completed puzzles, and told the recruiters about her love of mathematics and English.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Hill |first=Alex |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=mZ-JEAAAQBAJ&dq=joan+joslin+bletchley+park&pg=PT86 |title=Centennials: The 12 Habits of Great, Enduring Organisations |date=2023-06-15 |publisher=Random House |isbn=978-1-5291-5917-2 |language=en}}</ref> After six weeks learning to use [[Tabulating machine|Hollerith machines]] for code-breaking, Joslin worked in Block C during the war to decrypt messages from Japanese airplanes and German ships.<ref name=":0" /> Her work helped locate and sink the [[German battleship Scharnhorst|German battleship ''Scharnhorst'']].<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |date=2005-05-31 |title='We had to keep the war's end secret' |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/1400384/We-had-to-keep-the-wars-end-secret.html |access-date=2025-04-14 |website=[[The Daily Telegraph|The Telegraph]] |language=en}}</ref>

A few days before [[Victory in Europe Day]], Joslin has said that "were on night duty and we had a message through that the German troops in Italy had capitulated and we realised that the war in Europe had ended. We were given 48 hours leave after we got the news." They had to keep the news secret.<ref name=":2" />

Joslin's cryptography work remained a secret until the mid-1970s.<ref name=":0" /> Her parents, her father-in-law and mother-in-law all died before they were allowed to know of Joslin's war work.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Adair |first1=Paula |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=XFjWDwAAQBAJ&dq=joan+joslin+bletchley+park&pg=PT103 |title=Key Stage 3 English Anthology: War |last2=Sheldon |first2=Jane |date=2021-02-08 |publisher=Hachette Learning |isbn=978-1-5104-7705-6 |language=en}}</ref>

Joslin was interviewed as part of the Bletchley Park Oral History Project in May 2014<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Roll of Honour |url=https://bletchleypark.org.uk/roll-of-honour/3530 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250221183849/https://bletchleypark.org.uk/roll-of-honour/3530/ |archive-date=2025-02-21 |access-date=2025-04-14 |website=Bletchley Park |language=en-GB}}</ref> and attended the reopening of the restored Bletchley Park centre by [[Catherine, Princess of Wales]] (then Duchess of Cambridge) in June 2014.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2014-06-18 |title=Duchess of Cambridge opens Bletchley Park restored centre |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-beds-bucks-herts-27898997 |access-date=2025-04-14 |work=BBC News |language=en-GB}}</ref> She also gave talks at local schools about her role during the war.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Woldingham remembers |url=https://www.woldinghamschool.co.uk/news-and-reviews/news/2020/11/12/woldingham-remembers/ |access-date=2025-04-14 |website=Woldingham School |language=en}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Joslin met her husband Kenneth Joslin on her first day of work at in Bletchley Park and they became engaged three years later, in 1944. They married on 9 August 1945 in [[Rugby, Warwickshire]], and were on honeymoon in [[Dover]] when the war in Japan ended.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Joan and Kenneth Joslin |url=http://www.stock.org.uk/memories/Joan_and_Kenneth_Joslin/Joan_and_Kenneth_Joslin_1.htm |access-date=2025-04-14 |website=The Village of Stock}}</ref> They lived in the village of [[Stock, Essex]].<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Rv6w-y-9xbs |title=Joan Joslin talking about her time at Bletchley |date=2015-11-15 |last=Stock Village |access-date=2025-04-14 |via=YouTube}}</ref>

== Death ==
Joslin died in [[Essex]] on 8 February 2020, at the age of 96. She is commemorated on the Bletchley Park  '''"'''CodeBreakers Wall'''."'''<ref name=":1" />
